requirements.statement: The CPH number question applies to every live-animal commodity except horses (0101), cats, dogs, ferrets and other live mammals (01061900), 05111000 and 05119985: cattle, pigs, sheep, goats, poultry, rabbits, camels, ostriches, parrots, reptiles, bees and fish all get it. Where it does not apply, the CPH page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a CPH number for every species kept on a holding, not only the few on today's list, and keeps the page out of reach for consignments that have no holding.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH question applies only when a commodity line's commodity is on the frontend's CPH commodity list (repo-frontend-p10-003): cattle bring it in and cats leave it out (trace-e2e-p6-068, trace-e2e-p6-070), but nothing shows pigs, sheep, goats, poultry and the rest on it, and no source shows what the page does when opened for a consignment it does not apply to.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page the CPH section is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number', described 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', sits after the place of destination, and before a number is saved offers the link 'Add a CPH number'.
requirements.why: The link text is Design Release 2.1's; today's bare 'Add' action reads as nothing on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading, description and position already match (trace-e2e-p6-071, trace-e2e-p6-072); the empty row's action is an 'Add' link with the hidden suffix ' county parish holding (cph) number' (trace-e2e-p6-073) instead of the link text 'Add a CPH number'.

requirements.statement: A saved CPH number is shown on the consignment addresses page and on the review page as county/parish/holding with slashes, such as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link back to the CPH page.
requirements.why: The slashed form is how traders read and check a CPH number, and it is how Design Release 2.1 shows it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page shows the saved number as nine bare digits, '123456789' (trace-e2e-p6-075); the Change link already exists (trace-e2e-p6-076).

requirements.statement: A valid CPH number is stored as nine bare digits, the three parts joined with no separators, and is split back 2/3/4 into its boxes when the page is shown again.
requirements.why: The stored shape is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: today's record, and every stored notification, holds nine digits, so only the display gains slashes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-038 and trace-animals-fit-p13-025: the frontend joins the parts and stores 123456789.

requirements.statement: The CPH page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the single h1 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)', and the browser title 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the page's identity.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-002, trace-animals-fit-p13-003 and trace-animals-fit-p13-004 show the same heading, caption and title today.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages show the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the content.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-023 and trace-e2e-p7-008: the journey strip with the Draft tag and reference is on the CPH and contact pages today; the permanent address page gets it when it is built.

requirements.statement: A collapsed 'What is a CPH number?' details component sits above the CPH inputs and, when opened, says 'A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled.'
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their CPH number need to know what it is before they look for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-007, repo-frontend-p10-008 and trace-animals-fit-p13-017 show the same summary and definition today.

requirements.statement: The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds a second place to find the number, but its link is a placeholder ('#'), so where it goes is not designed.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the paragraph ends after '(APHA).' with no GOV.UK clause or link (repo-frontend-p10-009, trace-animals-fit-p13-018).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is asked as one fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number', not as a heading.
requirements.why: One question, one legend, so the page keeps a single h1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-011 and trace-animals-fit-p13-006: a role=group fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number' today.

requirements.statement: The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and describes the whole group.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's wording of the hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint reads 'For example, 12/345/6789.', with a comma and a full stop (repo-frontend-p10-012, trace-animals-fit-p13-007); it already describes the group and never shows 123/456/789.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes in one row, laid out with the GOV.UK date-input pattern, with visible labels 'County' (2 wide, at most 2 characters), 'Parish' (3 wide, at most 3) and 'Holding number' (4 wide, at most 4), each asking for a numeric keypad.
requirements.why: A CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits; boxes sized to the parts make each part easy to enter and check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-014 to repo-frontend-p10-020 and trace-animals-fit-p13-010 to trace-animals-fit-p13-015: the same three labelled, sized boxes in the date-input layout today.

requirements.statement: Each CPH box has autocomplete turned off and the pattern [0-9]* as well as the numeric input mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets both so browsers do not offer unrelated saved values and phones show the digit keypad.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each box has inputmode numeric and spellcheck off, but no autocomplete=off and no pattern (repo-frontend-p10-017, trace-animals-fit-p13-014).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, each CPH box drops any non-digit as the trader types and stops at its maximum length.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps stray characters out of the boxes as they are typed; the server checks stay as the backstop.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the boxes are plain text inputs with no script (trace-animals-fit-p13-014 shows the attributes only), and non-digits are caught only on save.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, pasting into a CPH box keeps only the digits and spreads them across that box and the ones after it (2, 3 then 4 digits), so pasting 123456789 or 12/345/6789 into County fills all three boxes.
requirements.why: Traders often copy the whole number from an APHA document; Design Release 2.1 lets one paste fill the three parts.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a whole slashed number pasted into County stays there and is rejected on save with 'County must be 2 digits' and the missing-part errors (repo-frontend-p10-033); without JavaScript that stays the case.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, focus moves to the next CPH box once a box is full, and Backspace in an empty box moves focus back to the previous box and deletes its last digit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 auto-advances between the boxes, but moving focus while the trader types is a change of context that accessibility guidance warns against.
requirements.deltaNote: Today nothing moves focus between the boxes.

requirements.statement: Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty raises no error: it saves no CPH number (clearing any saved before), the trader moves on, and the CPH section stays incomplete, so the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader move on and holds the gap at submission instead; required-to-proceed is a design choice the prototype can express, not a constraint it cannot.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an empty submit is refused with 400 and the single error 'Enter a CPH number' linked to the County box.

requirements.statement: A partly filled or wrongly formed CPH number is refused with one error per wrong part, in county, parish, holding order: 'Enter the county', 'Enter the parish' or 'Enter the holding number' for a missing part; 'County must be 2 digits', 'Parish must be 3 digits' or 'Holding number must be 4 digits' for a wrong length; 'County must only contain numbers', 'Parish must only contain numbers' or 'Holding number must only contain numbers' for a non-digit. Parts are trimmed first, and a whole slashed number typed into one box is refused.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 silently drops a part-entered number, which loses what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-023 to repo-frontend-p10-033 and trace-animals-fit-p13-035 to trace-animals-fit-p13-041: these per-part messages are the frontend's today.

requirements.statement: CPH errors re-render the page with status 400 and every typed value kept: an error summary titled 'There is a problem' links each error to its box and moves focus there, one inline message on the whole question lists every error (with a hidden 'Error:' prefix, between the hint and the boxes), each wrong box gets the error border, and the group's description includes the error.
requirements.why: A three-part question needs one message on the question and a border on each wrong part, so the trader sees which part to fix.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-034 to repo-frontend-p10-037 and trace-animals-fit-p13-042: the error presentation is the frontend's today.

requirements.statement: A stored CPH number that is not nine digits is flagged on the page with 'The saved CPH number is no longer valid. Re-enter the county, parish and holding numbers.', linked to the County box, with all three boxes shown empty.
requirements.why: Stored data can predate today's rules; the trader is told to re-enter it rather than shown stray digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-041 and repo-frontend-p10-042.

requirements.statement: The CPH page opens with three empty boxes when nothing is saved, and with the saved parts filled back in (County 12, Parish 345, Holding number 6789) when a number is saved, however the page is reached.
requirements.why: The trader can check and change what they entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-039, repo-frontend-p10-040 and trace-e2e-p6-077.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link goes to the addresses page only when reached with return=addresses (repo-frontend-p10-043, trace-e2e-p6-078); reached any other way it goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: The CPH and contact address forms post back to their own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and a failed save re-renders the page with status 500, the recoverable-error banner and the trader's values kept.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in their error states, and each radio group's description names its hint and, on error, its error.

It applies only when the consignment holds commodity 01061900 with at least one species that needs a permanent address; otherwise the page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The address fields leave the animal identification form.

requirements.why: The contact must be one of the trader's own branches, so the page tells them how to add a missing branch.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a paragraph link 'Add a new address' sits above the heading, before the fieldset (trace-e2e-p7-031, trace-e2e-p8-075).
requirements.blockedBy: Rhys lifts his 2026-09-04 address-space block on DR1 inc-053 with a fresh ruling, once the team's live address work settles.

requirements.statement: The contact page's add link opens the address book's add-address page set to add a branch address, and the address book returns the trader to the contact page when the address is saved.
requirements.why: The new address must be a branch address to appear in the contact list, and the copy promises a return to this page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the link goes to the INS address book's add page through the handshake (journey-type gbn-ag, notification-id, fulfilment-id, handshake-token) with no address type and no return path of its own (trace-e2e-p7-032, trace-e2e-p7-080).
requirements.blockedBy: Rhys lifts his 2026-09-04 address-space block on DR1 inc-053 with a fresh ruling, once the team's live address work settles.

requirements.statement: Back on the contact page after adding a branch address, the new address is in the list, selected as the contact address, and the page shows the success banner '<name> address added to your address book' once.
requirements.why: The trader added the address to use it here, so it is chosen for them and they are told it was saved.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows the contact page after the add handshake returns successfully.
requirements.blockedBy: Rhys lifts his 2026-09-04 address-space block on DR1 inc-053 with a fresh ruling, once the team's live address work settles.

requirements.statement: Coming back from the address book add with a not-found error, the contact page shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' in the error summary; with an unavailable error it shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.' and the recoverable-error state.
requirements.why: The round trip to the address book crosses services and can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-069 and repo-frontend-p10-070.

requirements.statement: When the animals frontend runs in stub mode, the contact page offers no link to add an address.
requirements.why: Stub mode has no address book to add to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-068 and trace-animals-fit-p12-048.

requirements.statement: The contact page offers only the signed-in organisation's own branch addresses, newest added first, not every record in its address book.
requirements.why: The contact is the trader's own branch responsible for the consignment in Great Britain; offering overseas consignors and other parties is a live defect DR1 recorded.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page lists every record in the organisation's address book, overseas ones included (13 in the fit stub, 28 end to end), newest first (trace-e2e-p7-014).

requirements.statement: Each contact address radio is labelled with the address's name and has its address lines, joined with commas, as its hint, without the country, such as '15 Union Street, Aberdeen, AB11 5BN'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's hint; branch addresses are all in Great Britain, so the country adds nothing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint ends with the country, joined with commas (repo-frontend-p10-062, trace-e2e-p7-011); the label is already the name (trace-e2e-p7-010).

requirements.statement: The contact addresses are one list of radios whose value is the address record's id, with no search box, no pagination and no manual entry of its own.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree: new contacts come only through the address book.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p7-012 and trace-e2e-p7-013: one unpaginated radio list keyed by record id today.

requirements.statement: No contact address is chosen when the page first opens; on return, the saved contact's radio is selected while it still matches a record in the list.
requirements.why: The trader makes the choice, and sees it again when they come back.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p7-017 and trace-e2e-p7-029.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the contact page with no address chosen shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, linked to the first radio, and saves nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 requires the contact address before the trader moves on to review.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving with nothing chosen is allowed, shows no error and exits to the overview with the task still 'To do'.

requirements.statement: Submitting a contact id that is not in the list shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, answers 400, selects no radio and saves nothing; the error link focuses the first radio.
requirements.why: A forged or stale choice must not be saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-071 and trace-animals-fit-p12-051 to trace-animals-fit-p12-053.

requirements.statement: Choosing a contact address and pressing 'Save and continue' saves it and goes to the review page ('Review your notification').
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address is the last step before review.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a saved contact redirects to the notification's overview, not the review page.

requirements.statement: The contact page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page, or to the review page when the page was opened from review.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact page follows the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: Opened from the hub or the review page, the contact page returns there after saving.
requirements.why: A trader changing one answer goes back to where they started.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-076: the page returns to the hub on 'Save and return to overview' and to check answers in a change visit today.

requirements.statement: Outside amend, the contact page ends with all three controls: 'Save and continue', a secondary button that saves and returns to the hub, and a link that cancels and returns to the hub.
requirements.why: The hub's task list links to the contact page, so under DR1's inc-161 rule (b) it keeps the three return controls, as Design Release 2.1 shows; the controls' wording is the journey-wide rename.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-081 and trace-e2e-p7-019 to trace-e2e-p7-021: the three controls are there today, labelled 'overview' where Design Release 2.1 says 'hub'.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the contact, CPH and permanent address pages show the amend controls: 'Save and return' (to the review page) and a secondary 'Save and continue', with no return-to-hub button or cancel link; the CPH page also offers the cancel-amend dialog.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends an amending trader back to review rather than to the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows these pages in an amend.

requirements.statement: The contact address task is reached from the hub row 'Contact address for this consignment' under '6. Contact address', is open at any time without the consignment addresses being done, and shows 'To do' until a contact is saved and 'Complete' after.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree the contact is not gated on the other sections.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p12-039, trace-animals-fit-p12-040 and trace-e2e-p7-004.

requirements.statement: A notification cannot be submitted without a contact address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 requires the contact address, and the consignment addresses, before submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the contact address is an obligation of the notification (repo-frontend-p10-055), but no today source shows a submit refused without one.

requirements.statement: Choosing a contact saves a copy of that address's name and address into the notification, remembering which record it came from; the held copy stays valid, and the task complete, even if the address-book record later changes or is deleted.
requirements.why: Copy semantics is a real persistence and cross-service constraint: the address book is another service, and a submitted notification must keep the address it was submitted with.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-074 and repo-frontend-p10-075: a copy with pickedFromId, never flagged invalid on return, today.

requirements.statement: Once a contact is held, the contact page shows a 'Current contact address' summary card below the radios with the contact's name and one-line address and an 'Edit details' link; with no contact held there is no card.
requirements.why: The notification holds a copy that can differ from every record in the list; the card is the only place it shows on this page. Design Release 2.1 has no such card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-064 and trace-e2e-p7-026: the card is there today.

requirements.statement: 'Edit details' opens /consignment/contact/edit, captioned 'Contact address for consignment' and prefilled; saving returns to the contact page, changes only this notification's copy (the address-book record is unchanged and no new record is added), leaves no radio selected, and the review's contact row shows the edited details.
requirements.why: A trader can correct the contact for one consignment without changing their address book. Design Release 2.1 has no way to edit the contact copy.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p5-078 to repo-tests-p5-081 and trace-e2e-p8-077 to trace-e2e-p8-080: editing the copy works this way today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's three seeded branch addresses (Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, West Country Livestock Ltd, Cymru Animal Imports Ltd) and their mismatched radio values are not reproduced; the real list comes from the organisation's address book.
requirements.why: They are prototype data, not the trader's own branches.

conflicts.about: Which return controls end the CPH page.

positions.says: Under inc-161 rule (b) the CPH page, reached from another page, ends with the primary button alone.
The CPH page offers 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
'Save and return to hub' on the CPH page saves the draft and goes to the hub.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's inc-161 judgement on this same difference wins (the 2026-10-07 ruling has a DR1 judgement override the prototype): the CPH page keeps 'Save and continue' alone, as it does today.

conflicts.about: Which return controls end the new permanent address page.

positions.says: Only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls; a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone.
The per-animal page offers 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's inc-161 rule (b) wins: the permanent address page is reached from the consignment addresses page, so it ends with 'Save and continue' alone, like the CPH page and the party pickers. The prototype's back link and 'Save and continue' destination still stand.

conflicts.about: How a CPH number is stored: with slashes (Design Release 2.1) or as nine bare digits (today).

positions.says: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
The CPH number is stored as one value county/parish/holding, such as 12/345/6789.
A valid CPH is stored as nine bare digits.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence constraint wins: the stored record stays nine digits, as today; only what the trader sees follows the prototype, so the addresses page and review show 12/345/6789.

conflicts.about: Whether the CPH page can be saved with all three boxes empty.

positions.says: Blank boxes save no CPH number and the user moves on without an error.
All three boxes empty shows 'Enter a CPH number'.
The CPH number is required: the page cannot be saved without one.
An empty submit shows 'Enter a CPH number' linked to County.
The CPH page refuses an empty submit with an error summary.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: required-to-proceed is a journey choice the prototype can express (it does on the contact page), not a constraint it cannot, so a blank save moves on and the CPH section stays incomplete until submission. The 'Enter a CPH number' empty-submit error goes.

conflicts.about: Whether a part-filled or wrongly formed CPH number is checked.

positions.says: Real validation the prototype cannot express overrides it.
A county-only CPH number is accepted with no error and silently not stored.
No validation error is asserted for a non-numeric or wrongly sized part.
Missing, wrong-length and non-digit parts each show their own error.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: format validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so today's per-part errors stay. prototype-dr2-1-source-p9-014 and p9-015 are not overruled: they still back the all-blank save (c-cph-permanent-and-contact-004).

conflicts.about: Where the CPH page's back link and 'Save and continue' go.

positions.says: 'Save and continue' returns to the roles and addresses page.
The back link goes to the roles and addresses page.
In the opening run, saving a valid CPH continues to the contact page.
Outside the opening run and without return context, saving goes to the hub.
In the opening run, 'Save and continue' redirects to the contact select page.
The page reached after the CPH number in the opening run is 'Contact address for consignment'.
Reached sequentially, saving returns to the notification overview.
Reached sequentially, the back link goes to the notification overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the CPH page's back link and 'Save and continue' always go to the consignment addresses page. trace-animals-fit-p13-027 is kept for the contact page's heading only, which still holds.

conflicts.about: Where 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes.

positions.says: 'Save and continue' on consignment addresses leads to the contact address page.
With a CPH-triggering line, the addresses page's 'Save and continue' goes to the CPH page.
With no CPH-triggering line, it goes straight to the overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the addresses page's 'Save and continue' goes on to the contact address page, and the CPH page is reached from its own section link.

conflicts.about: Where the CPH help's 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' link goes.

positions.says: The help adds 'or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK', but the link is a placeholder with href '#'.
The help names APHA documents only, with no link.

conflicts.outcome: Design Release 2.1 asks for a link it does not give a destination for, so it cannot be built as written.
conflicts.question: Which page should the CPH help's 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' link open?
conflicts.default: Add the clause, linking to GOV.UK's 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number), in English and Welsh.

conflicts.about: Whether the CPH boxes move focus by themselves as the trader types.

positions.says: Focus moves to the next box once a box is full.
Backspace in an empty box moves focus back and deletes the previous box's last digit.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it; the list given may be examples or complete.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, but moving focus on input is a change of context under WCAG 2.2 success criterion 3.2.2, an accessibility constraint the ruling's list does not clearly name; the two readings build different pages.
conflicts.question: Should the CPH boxes move focus by themselves (forward when full, back on Backspace), as Design Release 2.1 does, despite accessibility guidance against auto-tabbing?
conflicts.default: Build the digit filtering and paste spreading, but not the automatic focus moves: the trader moves between boxes with Tab as today.

conflicts.about: Whether the permanent address page and its same-as-destination choice are built now, given DR1's address-space block.

positions.says: inc-057 (the permanent address as its own step) is blocked by Rhys's 2026-09-04 address-space ruling.
inc-058 (reusing the place of destination) is blocked by the same ruling.
inc-057 and inc-058 are blocked until the team's address work settles, and none may be built without a fresh ruling.
The permanent address is its own per-animal page in the consignment parties section.
Today the permanent address is a block inside the animal identification form.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's judgement on this same difference is followed: it deferred the change rather than rejecting it, pending a fresh ruling from Rhys once the address work settles. So Design Release 2.1's page and choice are adopted as the target, blocked on that ruling. Field-level changes (labels, warning, order) are not blocked, as DR1 left inc-009, inc-059 and inc-066 buildable.

conflicts.about: Whether the contact page's guidance sentence, structure and add-a-branch path are built now, given DR1's address-space block.

positions.says: inc-046 and inc-053, which change the contact page, are blocked by Rhys's 2026-09-04 ruling.
inc-046 (contact page guidance) is blocked because address work is being done in this space now.
The page opens with the 'person responsible for the consignment' sentence.
Under 'Select an address' the page tells the trader to add a new branch address.
The page carries the hint 'Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.'
Outside stub mode the page shows an 'Add a new address' link above the form.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's deferral of inc-046 and inc-053 is followed: Design Release 2.1's sentence, 'Select an address' structure and add-a-branch path are the target, blocked on Rhys's fresh ruling once the address work settles.

conflicts.about: Which addresses the contact page offers: own branch addresses only, or the whole address book.

positions.says: Offering overseas consignors where DR1 offers only GB branch addresses is a live defect, to fix once the typed address-book record lands.
The contact options are the organisation's branch (or contact) addresses.
The page offers one radio per entry in the organisation's address book.
The list offers addresses of any country.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins, and DR1's judgement agrees on the target: only the organisation's own branch addresses. DR1 deferred it until an address-book record carries a type; that typed record is within this programme (address-book-add-and-edit), so the change is built once it lands rather than blocked.

conflicts.about: Whether the contact page can be saved with no address chosen.

positions.says: Submitting without choosing shows 'Select a contact address'.
Submitting with no radio selected is not an error and the trader moves on.
Saving with no contact address selected is allowed and exits to the hub.
An empty save shows no error and exits to the overview.
After an empty save the task stays 'To do' with no banner or error.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: 'Save and continue' with nothing chosen shows 'Select a contact address'.

conflicts.about: Where the contact page's back link and 'Save and continue' go.

positions.says: 'Save and continue' goes to the review page.
The back link goes to review when opened from review, otherwise to the consignment addresses page.
The back link goes to the notification hub.
Saving a valid contact redirects to the overview hub.
The back link lands on the overview hub.
Saving returns to the overview, not a next question.
The back link goes to the overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: 'Save and continue' goes to the review page, and the back link to the consignment addresses page (or review when opened from review).

conflicts.about: Whether the contact task stays complete when the chosen address-book record no longer exists.

positions.says: Persistence and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express override it.
The contact task is complete only while the saved address still exists in the list.
A held contact copy is never flagged invalid on return.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the notification holds a copy of the contact, so it stays complete when the address-book record (in another service) changes or goes, as today.

conflicts.about: Whether the contact page keeps today's 'Current contact address' card and editing of the contact copy, which Design Release 2.1 does not have.

positions.says: The contact page is the radios list alone, with no card and no way to edit the chosen contact.
A 'Current contact address' card with 'Edit details' shows the held copy.
Editing the contact copy from the contact page changes only this notification.
The ruling does not say whether a feature Design Release 2.1 does not show at all is removed or left alone.

conflicts.outcome: No ruling settles whether a feature the prototype lacks is a difference to remove, and the stored copy (a persistence constraint) can differ from every listed record, so removing the card would hide it.
conflicts.question: Should the contact page keep today's 'Current contact address' card and its 'Edit details' for the notification's copy, which Design Release 2.1 does not have?
conflicts.default: Keep the card and editing as they are today, placed below the Design Release 2.1 radios, so an edited contact that matches no listed record still shows.

conflicts.about: Whether a new permanent address keeps its county and its fields in place on return.

positions.says: Persistence constraints the prototype cannot express override it.
The county entered on a new permanent address is not saved.
With no address line 2, revisiting shows the town under line 2 and the postcode under town.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the real service saves every field, county included, and reads each back into its own field; the prototype's data loss is not copied.
